$comment: Per-model OUTPUT-token caps applied by apply-capability-overrides.ps1 through the
management route PATCH /api/model-capability-overrides {target, key, value} with
key = "max_output_tokens". This is the exact analogue of context-overrides.json
(which uses key = "context_length"): a manual row wins over the gateway's own
resolution, so add a row only where the gateway would otherwise forward an
over-limit max_tokens and the upstream rejects the whole request.
TARGET SPELLING: use the RESOLVED provider, not the routing alias. The gateway
builds the override lookup key from the resolved provider (server.js
getModelCapabilityOverride), e.g. the routing alias scw resolves to provider
scaleway, so the row must read scaleway/qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507 - a row
spelled scw/... does NOT match and silently does nothing.
NOTE: the cap alone only makes the gateway FILTER an over-limit leg out of a combo
(HARD_COMPAT_REASONS includes output_tokens); it does not CLAMP the forwarded value.
Clamping is the code change in patches/0001-clamp-max-tokens.patch. Keep both.

overrides.$comment: Scaleway rejects max_completion_tokens > 16384 with a 400 payload validation error ("max_completion_tokens is limited to 16384 for qwen3-235b-a22b-instruct-2507") and the whole request fails, so the combo falls through. Measured 2026-09-30: max_tokens=32768 -> 400, max_tokens=16 -> 200. The cap lets the request be clamped to 16384 instead of rejected. Row already applied live at 2026-09-30 14:32:21Z; this file is the durable source.
